pilot.summary: Three-player pod at Tom's, me on Edgar, Alex on Sauron, Tom on blue-black. Five vampires down by turn three off three mana spent, and the whole table made Markov the problem immediately — I ate multiple wipes and a stack of counters, and rebuilt in a turn or two every time. I did not cast Edgar until I had eight mana, which is my own mistake; when he landed it was the finisher, and Olivia's Wrath into a wide haste swing got Alex to 1. Tom countered Champion of Dusk and Bloodthirsty Conqueror, I needed one more vampire, and had nothing.

Five-player pod at Oliver's, second game of the night, seat 5. Mulliganed once and kept a two-land hand out of stubbornness — I knew at the time it should have gone back. Blood Artist and Bloodthirsty Conqueror landed early and a wipe with the drain online killed eleven creatures: every opponent lost 11, I gained 11, and I was around 50 to the table's 20. Then Ryan's recurring artifact and enchantment removal picked off Anointed Procession and the rest, I ran out of steam with vampires on board and nothing in hand, and Deflecting Swat and Teferi's Protection sat uncast all game because the mana was always spent on vampires.

Three-player pod at Alex's in Orinda, game two of four, me against Alex and Stuart. "Best-case opener and it did not matter" — two lands plus Sol Ring into a Talisman, four mana on turn one, Edgar down fast, Warleader's Call and the token-enters enchantments in place — and then Edgar was the only vampire I cast all game. Got Alex to 12 commander damage before he assembled blockers and he closed later with an oversized threat; I ran out of steam on card draw again. The conversation with Alex afterwards is the part that matters: the deck changes direction from swarm typal to lords and payoffs, tokens become the dig engine, and the token-conversion axis from 25 August is withdrawn.

Five-player pod at Oliver's, game three of three, first night on the twelve-swap list. Tom's Goblin Sharpshooter pinged my tokens and that fed the card-draw creatures, so I was running my engine off his removal. I resolved a big flyer that draws cards, brought Edgar down, then pivoted to Bloodletter of Aclazotz for the doubled damage and swung lethal into Alex to take him out. Tom tutored a two-card infinite and closed before my lethal resolved — a loss with Edgar dominating the board, and one I want on record as unsatisfying in a way that losing to a better board is not.

Four-player pod at Alex's, first of two games on the night: me on Edgar, Oliver on Vito mono-black vampires, Tom on Purphoros mono-red goblin ETB, Alex on an Azorius counters deck. Strong opener — Viscera Seer turn one off a swamp for the eminence token and its sac ability used early, never missed a land drop, Elspeth out, then Edgar off Ancient Tomb on turn five — and early vampires plus Edgar swinging held momentum all game; Oliver said afterwards he was always a turn behind. I went too all-in on Tom with Elspeth exposed, she got taken down, and Tom's Purphoros ETB pings finished the job before my lethal landed, about an hour in. The two lessons I wrote down: once a planeswalker is online, keep blockers up and protect the engine before pushing tempo; and Purphoros is the natural predator for mid-range aggro, so the deck needs targeted disruption in white.

Four-player pod at Oliver's, first of two games, Tom in India: me on Edgar, Ryan on Teval, Oliver on a blue-black mill deck, Alex on his spaceships novelty deck. I ate board wipe after board wipe and rebuilt fast each time, but only into small blockers, and by turn eight, nine, ten I did not have enough cards in hand to play things. I played Vish Kal too early and did not hit Blood Artist until mid-game, so the wipes came with neither doing its job; Markov came down, I swung into a wider board with bigger +1/+1 counters, and could not convert before the next wipe. At one point I could have made a 12/12 flying lifelink with Vish Kal and Vito on board, but I went after Alex, who had indestructible creatures; we worked him to about seven, Oliver almost milled him out, and I sat there in my vampire nest — no result filed for this game, cause filed as wipe.

At Steven's, a four-player pod, game one of two, on v3.0.0. This was the first Vampires win and the first game since the v3.0 refactor. Steven's Magda got off fast (treasures, a tutor for Utvara Hellkite, a stack of 6/6 flyers) and led 38 to 20 while Stuart stalled on three lands and David's deck was too slow to matter. Life gain and drain kept me in it while the tokens built a board. Then Ashnod's Altar turned tokens into mana for Crossway Troublemakers, the wide swing cost Steven his dragons, more Altar mana brought out Edgar, and Steven died mostly to Blood Artist and targeted damage. I don't recall the exact last sequence.

read.what_it_does: On v3.0.0, the list I am holding, cheap vampires and Edgar's eminence tokens are the fodder, and three converters turn them into something on the table: Blood Artist into drain, Crossway Troublemakers into attackers that kill blockers, Ashnod's Altar into a mana burst (008). Charismatic Conqueror kept handing me 1/1 lifelink tokens because the table wanted blockers, and Caretaker's Talent drew a card off tokens entering, so the board and the hand both grew from the same tokens (008). That is the identity I wrote down the day before the game, 'Vampires are the FUEL, not the engine' (007), and one game (008) is all the current list has behind it.
read.how_it_plays: It does not look like it is winning until it is. On 008 I was down 20 to 38 against Steven's Magda and a stack of 6/6 flyers, life gain and drain kept me in it while the token board built, and the game turned on the one turn Ashnod's Altar landed (008). Edgar stayed in the command zone making tokens and was cast only at the end, off Altar mana, as the finisher (008). On older lists the table made Markov the archenemy from turn three and wiped it again and again: on V1 (001, 002) and on v1.1.1 (006). 008 records no wipe, but Stuart was stuck on three lands and David was too slow to matter, so that one game does not say the table has stopped wiping. Where it ended: a win on 008. Every logged game before it was a loss or had no result filed, either ahead on board and beaten by another seat's clock (004, 005, on v1.1.0) or out of cards (006, on v1.1.1).
mindful_of: The close ran through Ashnod's Altar. Its mana cast Crossway Troublemakers and then Edgar on the same closing run, and I do not recall the exact final sequence, so I cannot repeat that line from memory yet (008).

Blood Artist is the converter that killed Steven, and my table note is 'remove Blood Artist early when it comes out' (008). Expect it to draw removal. On v1.1.1 I did not hit it until mid-game and then lost it to a wipe, so sequence it for the wipe, not before it (006).

Vish Kal went down too early on v1.1.1, and the 12/12 flying lifelink it could have made with Vito on the board went at Alex, who had indestructible creatures. Don't swing the big lifelinker into the indestructible board (006). Vish Kal and Vito are both still in the 99.

Running out of steam was how the deck lost on every earlier list that was played: vampires on board and nothing in hand on V1 (001, 002, 003), and again on v1.1.1 by turn eight to ten (006). On 008 the draw ran off tokens entering through Caretaker's Talent. One game does not settle whether that is fixed.
A fast seat sets the clock. Magda set the pace of that pod and was at 38 to my 20 before the converters arrived (008). On v1.1.0, Tom's Purphoros ETB pings got there before my lethal did (005).

Protection that stays in hand is no protection. On V1, Deflecting Swat and Teferi's Protection sat uncast all game because my mana went into casting vampires (002). On v1.1.1 the deck was 'super creature heavy' with 'not a lot of protection' (006). Both cards are still in the 99.

Protect a planeswalker before pushing tempo. On v1.1.0 I went all-in on Tom with Elspeth exposed and she was taken down (005). On V1 she was targeted the moment she landed (001). She is still in the 99.
Swing lethal when it's there, at the right player. Both v1.1.0 losses came with lethal in sight (004, 005), and on v1.1.1 the momentum turn went into the indestructible board (006).

Edgar's cast is a decision, not what happens with spare mana. On V1 I did not cast him until eight mana because I was not thinking about him (001). On 008 casting him late off Altar mana was the plan and it closed the game (008).

Ryan's recurring artifact and enchantment removal picks off Anointed Procession. It resolved and was gone the following turn on V1 (002), and on v1.1.1 it was 'a great card, hard to get off' (006). Procession is still in the 99.
Mulligan discipline. On V1 I took one mulligan and then kept a two-land hand out of stubbornness, knowing at the time it should go back (002).
Pay the life. On v1.1.0 I missed paying more life to pump a vampire while it was still on the battlefield, and lost a pile of extra cards off the death trigger (004).
Seat 5 in a five-player pod. My read is that the first-seat momentum advantage compounds with a mana deficit instead of just adding to it (002, on V1).
read.what_changed: v3.0.0 is the bracket3-v1 branch merged 2026-11-10, 'bracket 4 to bracket 3'. Out: Ancient Tomb, Enlightened Tutor, Bloodthirsty Conqueror and Exquisite Blood. In: Grim Haruspex, Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet, Midnight Reaper and a Swamp. My note on 008 says v3.0 cut Sanguine Bond. It did not, and Sanguine Bond is still in the 99. None of the four cuts or three adds is named in 008, so the game says nothing about them card by card. 008 is the first logged game since 006 on v1.1.1. Nothing was played on v2.0.0 or v2.1.0, the bracket-4 lists in between, so the win is evidence for the list as it stands and cannot be credited to the v3.0 cuts alone. My own read after the game: before v3.0 the deck went wide with middling vampires and tried to win through combat damage, and now the tokens convert into different kinds of value: 'it validates our recent refactoring' (008). That is the direction I asked for on v1.1.1, life gain and drain as the engine, with damage that is not combat damage (006), and the identity note's 'Vampires are the FUEL, not the engine' (007). Superseded: the lords-and-payoffs direction from V1 (003) was true of the deck it was read against, and the converter read replaces it. These lessons are about cards this deck no longer runs and stay out of the read: the counters on Champion of Dusk and Bloodthirsty Conqueror (001), the Conqueror drain (002), and Edgar off Ancient Tomb on turn five (005).
